topics.focus: How to reduce lockout risks when changing Proxmox VE networking, without providing unsafe universal commands

sources.name: Proxmox VE official network configuration guide

facts.text: Proxmox VE uses Linux bridges for connecting guests to physical networks; bridge interfaces are often named vmbr0 or vmbr1.
The Proxmox VE graphical interface stages networking changes in /etc/network/interfaces.new rather than changing /etc/network/interfaces immediately.
With ifupdown2, the interface can apply staged network changes without restarting the entire host. This is not a guarantee that connectivity stays available.
Incorrect changes to a host's network can make it unreachable. An out-of-band management plan or console access reduces recovery risk.
The Proxmox VE documentation warns against indiscriminate use of traditional ifup and ifdown commands because they may interrupt guest traffic.

topics.focus: Explain persistent Docker storage choices without destructive cleanup instructions

facts.text: Docker volumes are managed by the Docker daemon and persist outside a container's writable layer.
Bind mounts expose a host path inside a container.
Bind mounts depend on the host's filesystem layout and can be less portable.
Bind mounts are writable by default; read-only mounts can limit changes.
Removing or pruning volumes can destroy persistent application data.

topics.focus: Explain how to plan, verify, and safely restore Docker volume backups

facts.text: Docker volumes exist independently of the lifecycle of an individual container.
Docker documentation provides examples for backing up and restoring volume contents.
Application-level consistency matters when planning backups of actively written data.
Restores should be tested in an isolated environment before replacing production data.
Deleting unused volumes may permanently remove application data.

topics.focus: Create a decision guide for Ubuntu Server backups and restore drills

facts.text: A backup plan should identify what data must be backed up.
A backup plan should determine how often backups are performed.
Backup plans should specify where copies are stored; off-site copies help with disaster recovery.
A backup plan should document how data is restored.
Multiple backup methods can improve resilience against data loss.

topics.focus: Explain how to reduce GitHub Actions token permissions without breaking CI

facts.text: GitHub recommends explicitly declaring minimum necessary GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permissions.
Workflows may have access to repository secrets or deployment credentials.
Pinning third-party actions to full commit SHAs mitigates mutable tag risks.
Organizations can restrict allowed actions through policy controls.
Changes to permissions should be tested against the workflow's required operations.

topics.focus: Describe practical secrets handling for GitHub Actions with no sample real credentials

facts.text: Repository and organization secrets can be configured through GitHub's Actions secrets settings.
Organization secrets can use repository access policies.
Secrets should not be included in committed workflow files or logs.
Credentials used by workflows should be scoped to the minimum required permissions.
GitHub warns that automatic redaction of transformed secret values is not guaranteed.
